History: Pamphylia was the coastal plain of southern Asia Minor. Pamphylians are named among the hearers at Pentecost; Paul landed at Perga in Pamphylia on his first journey, and John Mark left the party there.
Culture: Greek coastal cities under Roman rule, with the temple of Artemis at Perga among their landmarks.
Religion: Pagan temples before conversion; Paul preached in the region on his first journey.
BibleConnection: Named among the Pentecost hearers; Paul's first journey passed through Pamphylia twice, landing at Perga and later returning through it.
